scope: Premise at 2c4e4bf2: 29 @Cron handlers (17 in key-cortex) run in every server process with no cross-process claim: the only Redis SET NX in apps/server/src is identity-password.service.ts:503, and there is no advisory lock or leader election (git grep 'redlock|pg_try_advisory|advisory_lock': none). title: The event-wiring ratchet covers the other direction: no new event may be emitted with nothing listening, bridged or registered as intentionally publish-only
scope: Premise at 2c4e4bf2: the listen-only direction is already ratcheted: event-wiring.spec.ts:88 'adds no new listener with no emitter', with a shrink-only KNOWN_DEAD list (:49 onward; booking.deleted first), built on analyseEventWiring (apps/server/scripts/event-wiring.ts). scope: Premise at 2c4e4bf2: the global BusinessEventInterceptor (app.module.ts:273) records every POST/PATCH/DELETE under a :businessId route with before = the request body and after = the response (business-event.interceptor.ts:205-240) plus metadata.ip; snapshots are redacted by field name only (redaction.ts:13-32), so a contact create/update stores name, email, phone and notes, with subjectType 'contact' and subjectId the contact id (inferEventMeta :278-298, extractSubjectId :259-270). D-25 puts the purge in v1, so a forgotten person's email and phone stay readable in the business's event log. Privacy defect, not cross-tenant exposure: P1. Change: inside the same purge transaction, after step 5, scrub business_events rows of the request's business that name the subject or a merged duplicate: subjectType 'contact' and subjectId in ids, or before/after whose top-level contactId is in ids (raw SQL with jsonb ->> because the JSON paths are not Prisma-filterable in one statement); set before and after to NULL and remove metadata.ip, keep the row (event type, action, actor, timestamps stay as evidence). Add businessEventsScrubbed to the forget_purged entry's erased counts, and narrow PURGE_NOT_SWEPT accordingly. The legacy repair path (repairLegacyPurge) gets the same step because it shares eraseForgottenContact. Rows the in-transaction scrub cannot reach: the interceptor writes its row after the handler returns (a tap on next.handle(), business-event.interceptor.ts:215-240), outside any transaction. (i) The forget request's own row (POST businesses/:businessId/contacts/:contactId/forget, contact-privacy.controller.ts:148-170) is written after requestForget has soft-deleted the contact (contact-privacy.service.ts:426-455), with subjectType 'contact' (inferEventMeta), subjectId the ContactForgetRequest id (extractSubjectId takes response.id, :261-270), before = the body {reason} and after = the request row (top-level contactId, reason), plus metadata.ip; (ii) a mutation on the subject whose handler finished before the purge committed can write its row after the purge transaction committed. Change (added): before it emits, BusinessEventInterceptor resolves the event's contact (subjectId when subjectType is 'contact', else the top-level contactId of before/after) and, when that contact has a ContactForgetRequest in status 'requested' (contactId is unique on that table) or no longer exists in the business, writes the row with before and after NULL and no metadata.ip (event type, action, actor, subject and timestamps kept); one indexed read by id and businessId, only for contact-bearing events. The in-transaction scrub still handles rows written before the request. Out of scope: events of retained records (invoices, quotes, bookings) whose snapshot names the person without a top-level contactId: the commit lists them as retained under the existing PURGE_RETAINED_BASIS and an owner question decides whether to scrub them; notes/tasks events whose subject is the note (subjectId = note id) are reached through their top-level contactId. Tenancy: every statement carries business_id = the request's business. Schema: none. Backfill: purges already completed are not re-run; a dry-run count of already-purged contacts with surviving business_events rows is reported in the RETURN, any scrub of them only on owner authority. scope: REC-SCOPE-GUARDS. title: Whole-business GDPR erasure needs a second, deliberate act and leaves a durable record (form set by the owner's answer)
scope: REC-TWO-KEY. DEPENDS ON THE OWNER'S ANSWER (OQ-30, drafted as G4 OQ-30): which form, and whether it is v1 at all; nothing is built before RR-OWNER-RULINGS-RECORD (dependency) records the answer as a ruling; under answer D the packet is moot. Premise (verified): POST api/admin/businesses/:businessId/gdpr-delete (apps/server/src/modules/admin-platform/admin-business.controller.ts:100-104), behind AuthGuard and AdminGuard (one SUPER_ADMIN role check, apps/server/src/core/auth/admin.guard.ts), calls GdprPurgeService.purgeBusiness at once: an IRREVERSIBLE erase of every row carrying the business id (the controller's own comment, :83-99). No confirmation, no second actor, no delay, and no durable record: the service writes only logger lines (gdpr-purge.service.ts:146, :162), and an audit row with a business foreign key would itself be erased. No web screen calls it (git grep gdpr in apps/web/src: nothing). The other bulk deletes are not catastrophic: contact bulk delete is a soft delete of at most 100 rows with an audit row each (crm.controller.ts:764-775, crm.service.ts:1925-1986), restorable from the trash. Change under the recommended answer (B): the endpoint records an erasure request (who, when, business id, the slug typed back as confirmation) and erases nothing; a second call, at least the cooling-off period later (owner sets it; 24 hours proposed), by a SUPER_ADMIN, confirms and runs the existing purgeBusiness unchanged; a cancel call voids a pending request; a request older than its expiry cannot be confirmed. Records go to a table with no business foreign key so they survive the erasure: AuthAuditLog rows (event names gdpr_erase_requested, gdpr_erase_confirmed, gdpr_erase_cancelled; Schema: none), or a new table if the owner prefers (then a schema change inside an owner-approved migration set, D-167). Under answer A the confirm must come from a different SUPER_ADMIN; under C only the durable record is added. Human authority: the erase stays a manual platform-admin act; KEY has no tool for it and gets none. The contact-level GDPR forget (D-25) is out of scope, as are KEY actions, payroll and bulk money actions (payroll is hidden in v1). Fixture prefix (pre-allocated in the plan's prefix table so parallel lanes add disjoint registry entries): v72y_ for gdpr-erasure-two-step.integration.test.ts. Register each as {prefix, owner, packet: 'V1-72 (RR-ERASE-BUSINESS-TWO-STEP)'} in fixture-prefixes.json.

GREEN (answer B): the request alone erases nothing; a confirm before the cooling-off is refused (409) and erases nothing; a confirm after it erases exactly what apps/server/test/gdpr-purge.integration.test.ts proves today (that suite stays green, unchanged); the request, confirm and cancel records survive the erasure; a cancelled or expired request cannot be confirmed; a wrong slug is refused; a non-admin is refused at every step (403); another business is untouched. title: V1-STATUS reports packets that have been ready for longer than a budget without landing (stall signal from main alone)
scope: The surviving idea of the safe-but-stuck loop research (issue #153 comment 6243355172, 2026-10-17: separate safety from liveness; report a stall when a runnable packet makes no phase transition within a budget). The worker/selector that research targeted was retired in the D-141 tie-off and replaced by OWNER-DIR-V1-STANDING-001 (D-222) plus scripts/agent-memory; this packet adds only the liveness signal to the generated status, nothing that acts on it. Premise at 2c4e4bf2: readyList (scripts/agent-memory/lib.mjs:141-163) lists packets whose dependencies are done but records no time; buildStatus (lib.mjs:166-) has mainDate and per-row evidence but no age; `git grep -i stall scripts/agent-memory` finds nothing. Change: each ready row gets ready_since (the newest evidence commit date among its dependencies, or the plan's snapshot date when it has none, or null when unknown) and stalled: true when main_commit_date minus ready_since exceeds a budget (default 14 days, constant in lib.mjs); renderStatusMd prints a short 'Ready but stalled' list. title: Google Suite and Microsoft OAuth use PKCE (S256), with the verifier derived from the signed state so no new store is needed
scope: Architecture risk register R26 (architecture/architecture-risks.md:73): Google and Microsoft OAuth do not use PKCE. Premise at 2c4e4bf2: the Google Suite authorize URL is built with client_id, redirect_uri, response_type, scope, access_type, include_granted_scopes, prompt and state only (apps/server/src/core/connectors/google-suite.service.ts:175-185) and the token exchange sends no code_verifier (:212-221); the Microsoft authorize URL (apps/server/src/modules/connect/microsoft-oauth.service.ts:60-69) and token exchange (:104-117) likewise; `git grep -i 'code_challenge|pkce' 2c4e4bf2 -- apps/server/src` finds only the Twitter flow (modules/social/social.controller.ts:392-393). Change: a small helper derives code_verifier = base64url(HMAC-SHA256(stateSecret, 'pkce:' + state.nonce)) (43+ chars, never sent to the browser) and code_challenge = base64url(SHA-256(verifier)); both authorize URLs add code_challenge and code_challenge_method=S256; both callbacks recompute the verifier from the verified state's nonce and send it in the token exchange. Because the verifier is derived from the already-signed, single-use state, no new store or schema is needed and the existing replay protection (acceptedStateNonces, google-suite.service.ts:116-122) is unchanged. The client secret stays (confidential client); PKCE is added, not substituted. Out of scope: Twitter (already PKCE), social and other OAuth flows (hidden modules), the D-42/D-43 Gmail rules (unchanged). Schema: none. Verify at build time that both providers accept S256 PKCE with a confidential web client (they document it); if either refuses, stop with a CONTRADICTION.
definition_of_done: RED: a new case in the Google Suite service spec asserts the authorize URL from buildAuthUrl carries code_challenge and code_challenge_method=S256, and that the token-exchange body (fetch mocked) carries a code_verifier whose SHA-256 base64url equals that challenge; it fails on main because neither parameter exists. The same pair of cases for MicrosoftOAuthService. GREEN: all four cases pass; oauth-pkce.spec.ts proves the verifier is deterministic for one nonce, differs across nonces, is 43-128 characters of the unreserved set, and is never present in the authorize URL; a negative control (callback with a state whose nonce was altered) is refused by the existing state verification before any token call; the existing Google Suite and Microsoft connect specs (including the D-42 GMAIL_OWNER_ONLY and D-43 cases) stay green; no real provider traffic in tests; server tsc and lint ratchet clean.

scope: Architecture risk register R35 and R53 (architecture/architecture-risks.md:82, :100). Premises at 2c4e4bf2: (1) exportContact builds the bundle through collectBundle, whose contact read is `findFirst({ where: { id: contactId, businessId } })` with no deletedAt condition (apps/server/src/modules/crm/privacy/contact-privacy.service.ts:244, :1005-1009), so a contact that was soft-deleted, including one inside a forget grace period (requestForget sets deletedAt, :427-431), can still be exported with all its notes, media, invoices and audit; (2) TransactionalEmailService.send enforces doNotContact through a tenant-scoped contact read that selects only doNotContact (apps/server/src/modules/notifications/transactional-email.service.ts:420-433), so a soft-deleted or forget-pending contact still receives transactional email. Change: exportContact refuses (409 CONTACT_DELETED) when the contact has deletedAt set; the transactional send gate also selects deletedAt and returns the existing suppressed/refused result for a deleted contact, exactly as it does for doNotContact. Human path: an owner who needs the data of a deleted contact restores it first (the existing restore or cancelForget path) and then exports. Out of scope: redacting audit before/after inside the bundle (R35's second suggestion; owner may raise it), campaign senders (already filter deleted contacts per their own queries; not changed). Tenancy: both reads stay business-scoped. Schema: none. title: Cancelling a forget request restores only what the forget request deleted
scope: Architecture risk register R54 (architecture/architecture-risks.md:101): forget request and cancel conflate a normal soft delete with the forget flow. Premise at 2c4e4bf2: requestForget reads the contact without a deletedAt condition and sets deletedAt to now inside its transaction (apps/server/src/modules/crm/privacy/contact-privacy.service.ts:405-431), overwriting any earlier deletedAt; cancelForget then sets deletedAt to null unconditionally (:495-506). So a contact a member deleted normally, then had a forget request opened and cancelled, comes back as a live contact that nobody restored. Change: requestForget records whether the contact was already deleted (in the forget request row's existing metadata/JSON field if one exists, else in the audit entry it already writes; no new column) and keeps an earlier deletedAt; cancelForget restores deletedAt to null only when the forget request was the deletion's source, otherwise leaves the earlier soft delete in place and says so in its result. Schema: none expected; if the forget request model has no field that can carry the flag, stop and report (a column would be a separate migration packet). Human path unchanged: the normal restore path still un-deletes a contact deliberately. Fixture prefix (pre-allocated in the plan's prefix table so parallel lanes add disjoint registry entries): v73a_ for forget-cancel-prior-delete.integration.test.ts. Register each as {prefix, owner, packet: 'V1-73 (RR-FORGET-CANCEL-KEEPS-PRIOR-DELETE)'} in fixture-prefixes.json.
